name: Andhra Pradesh
overview: Andhra Pradesh runs along nearly a thousand kilometres of the Bay of Bengal coast. It is home to Tirumala, one of the most visited pilgrimage sites in the world, the Buddhist remains of Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda, the Araku Valley's coffee hills and the beaches of Visakhapatnam.
bestTime: October to March, when the coast is pleasant and dry.

name: Arunachal Pradesh
overview: India's easternmost state, where the sun rises first over the country. Arunachal is a land of high Himalayan passes, dense forests and over two dozen major tribes. Highlights include the 17th-century Tawang Monastery, the Ziro Valley's rice fields and music festival, and Namdapha National Park. Visitors need an Inner Line Permit.
bestTime: October to April; March–May for rhododendrons and clear passes.

name: Assam
overview: The gateway to the Northeast, shaped by the mighty Brahmaputra. Assam is known for its tea gardens, the one-horned rhinoceros of Kaziranga, the river island of Majuli and the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati. Bihu, the harvest festival, is its biggest celebration.
bestTime: November to April; Kaziranga is open roughly November to April.

name: Bihar
overview: Bihar is where much of ancient Indian history happened. The Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, the ruins of Nalanda University once drew scholars from across Asia, and Pataliputra (today's Patna) was the capital of the Maurya Empire. It is also sacred to Jains and Sikhs.
bestTime: October to March.

name: Chhattisgarh
overview: Over forty percent of Chhattisgarh is forest. The state is known for the wide Chitrakote Falls, often called India's Niagara, the tribal culture and crafts of Bastar, ancient temples at Sirpur and Bhoramdeo, and national parks such as Kanger Valley.
bestTime: July to February; waterfalls are at their fullest after the monsoon.

name: Goa
overview: India's smallest state by area, Goa blends beaches and nightlife with four and a half centuries of Portuguese influence. Its whitewashed churches in Old Goa are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and inland you'll find spice farms, wildlife sanctuaries and the Dudhsagar Falls.
bestTime: November to February; monsoon (June–September) is lush but rough at sea.

name: Gujarat
overview: Gujarat has the white salt desert of the Rann of Kutch, Gir Forest (the last home of the Asiatic lion), the Statue of Unity, and the Somnath and Dwarka temples. Its historic city of Ahmedabad was India's first UNESCO World Heritage City, and the state hosts nine nights of Navratri dancing every autumn.
bestTime: November to February; the Rann Utsav runs through winter.

name: Haryana
overview: Haryana surrounds Delhi on three sides. Kurukshetra, where the Mahabharata war is said to have been fought and the Bhagavad Gita spoken, draws pilgrims year-round. The state also has the Mughal-era Pinjore Gardens, the Sultanpur bird sanctuary and the Surajkund crafts fair.
bestTime: October to March.

name: Himachal Pradesh
overview: A mountain state of snow peaks, apple orchards and deodar forests. Himachal offers hill stations like Shimla and Manali, the Tibetan culture of McLeod Ganj, the cold desert of Spiti, and some of India's best paragliding, trekking and skiing.
bestTime: March to June for pleasant weather; December to February for snow.

name: Jharkhand
overview: Jharkhand, the 'land of forests', sits on the Chota Nagpur Plateau. Waterfalls such as Hundru and Dassam surround Ranchi, Betla National Park shelters elephants and tigers, and Deoghar's Baidyanath Dham is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas.
bestTime: October to March; waterfalls are best just after the monsoon.

name: Karnataka
overview: Karnataka ranges from the Vijayanagara ruins of Hampi and the royal city of Mysuru to the coffee hills of Coorg and the beaches of Gokarna. Its temples at Badami, Aihole, Belur and Halebidu are among the finest in stone, and Bengaluru is India's technology capital.
bestTime: October to March.

name: Kerala
overview: Kerala is a narrow green strip between the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats. Travellers come for houseboat cruises on the backwaters, tea estates in Munnar, the beaches of Varkala and Kovalam, Ayurveda, Kathakali dance, and spice-trade history in Fort Kochi.
bestTime: September to March; monsoon (June–August) is popular for Ayurveda.

name: Madhya Pradesh
overview: The 'heart of India' holds three UNESCO World Heritage Sites (the Khajuraho temples, the Sanchi stupa and the Bhimbetka rock shelters) as well as Orchha, Gwalior Fort and the Mahakaleshwar temple in Ujjain. Its tiger reserves, including Kanha and Bandhavgarh, are among India's best.
bestTime: October to March; tiger reserves are open October to June.

name: Maharashtra
overview: Maharashtra holds the city of Mumbai, the rock-cut caves of Ajanta and Ellora, and hundreds of hill forts linked to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. The Sahyadri hills come alive in the monsoon with waterfalls and treks, and pilgrims visit Shirdi, Pandharpur and Nashik.
bestTime: October to March; June to September for monsoon treks.

name: Manipur
overview: Manipur, the 'jewel of India', is ringed by hills around a central valley. Loktak Lake, with its floating phumdis and Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park, is its best-known sight. The state is also the home of Manipuri classical dance and of polo.
bestTime: October to April. Check current travel advisories before planning.

name: Meghalaya
overview: Meghalaya, the 'abode of clouds', includes some of the wettest places on earth. Its Khasi and Jaintia hills hold living root bridges grown from rubber fig trees, tall waterfalls, limestone caves and the crystal-clear Umngot River. Shillong is a lively hill capital with a strong music scene.
bestTime: October to April for treks; June to September for monsoon waterfalls.

name: Mizoram
overview: A state of steep bamboo-covered hills, Mizoram has a close-knit culture known for its bamboo dance, Cheraw. Travellers visit Aizawl's hillside streets, Phawngpui (Blue Mountain), the state's highest peak, and the quiet lake at Tam Dil. An Inner Line Permit is required.
bestTime: October to March.

name: Nagaland
overview: Nagaland is home to more than a dozen Naga tribes, each with its own dress, songs and festivals. The Hornbill Festival in December brings them together near Kohima. Other highlights are the Second World War cemetery at Kohima and the Dzukou Valley trek. An Inner Line Permit is required.
bestTime: October to May; early December for the Hornbill Festival.

name: Odisha
overview: Odisha's golden triangle of Bhubaneswar, Puri and Konark covers temple cities, the Jagannath Rath Yatra and the UNESCO-listed Sun Temple. Beyond it lie Chilika Lake, India's largest coastal lagoon, Olive Ridley turtle nesting beaches, and the tribal markets of Koraput.
bestTime: October to March; Rath Yatra falls in June or July.

name: Punjab
overview: Punjab, the 'land of five rivers', is the heartland of Sikhism. The Golden Temple in Amritsar welcomes visitors of every faith and serves free meals to tens of thousands each day. The state is also known for the Wagah border ceremony, the Jallianwala Bagh memorial, bhangra and generous food.
bestTime: October to March.

name: Rajasthan
overview: India's largest state is the land of maharajas: hill forts, lake palaces, painted havelis and the golden dunes of the Thar Desert. Jaipur, Udaipur, Jodhpur and Jaisalmer are each known by a colour, and six of its hill forts are together a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
bestTime: October to March; summers are very hot.

name: Sikkim
overview: Sikkim sits beneath Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest mountain. This small Himalayan state has Buddhist monasteries such as Rumtek and Pemayangtse, the high-altitude Tsomgo and Gurudongmar lakes, and Khangchendzonga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It was India's first fully organic state.
bestTime: March to May and October to December.

name: Tamil Nadu
overview: Tamil Nadu is a land of towering temple gateways and an unbroken classical tradition. Highlights include the Chola temples of Thanjavur, Madurai's Meenakshi Temple, the shore monuments of Mamallapuram, the hill station of Ooty, and Kanyakumari at the southern tip of mainland India.
bestTime: November to February; the hills are pleasant from March to June.

name: Telangana
overview: Telangana's capital Hyderabad mixes Qutb Shahi and Nizam-era monuments such as the Charminar and Golconda Fort with a modern tech city and its famous biryani. The Kakatiya-era Ramappa Temple near Warangal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
bestTime: October to February.

name: Tripura
overview: Tripura is a small hill state bordered on three sides by Bangladesh. It is known for the Ujjayanta Palace in Agartala, the lake palace of Neermahal, the giant rock carvings of Unakoti, and the Tripura Sundari Temple, one of the Shakti Peethas.
bestTime: October to March.

name: Uttar Pradesh
overview: Uttar Pradesh has the Taj Mahal, the ghats of Varanasi, the Buddhist site of Sarnath, the Nawabi culture of Lucknow, and Prayagraj, host of the Kumbh Mela. Mathura and Vrindavan, linked with Lord Krishna, draw crowds at Holi.
bestTime: October to March.

name: Uttarakhand
overview: Uttarakhand, 'Dev Bhoomi' or land of the gods, contains the Char Dham pilgrimage (Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, Badrinath), the yoga town of Rishikesh, the hill stations of Mussoorie and Nainital, Jim Corbett National Park and the Valley of Flowers.
bestTime: March to June and September to November; the Char Dham shrines open from about May to November.

name: West Bengal
overview: West Bengal stretches from the Darjeeling Himalaya to the Sundarbans mangroves, home of the Royal Bengal tiger. In between are Kolkata, a city of colonial landmarks, literature and Durga Puja, the terracotta temples of Bishnupur, and the toy train of the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway.
bestTime: October to March; Darjeeling is also pleasant from April to June.

name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
overview: A chain of tropical islands in the Bay of Bengal with white-sand beaches, coral reefs and rainforest. Visitors come for Radhanagar Beach on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock), scuba diving and snorkelling, and the Cellular Jail in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), a memorial to the freedom struggle.
bestTime: November to May; the sea is calmest from December to April.

name: Chandigarh
overview: Chandigarh, planned by Le Corbusier in the 1950s, is one of India's first planned cities and the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana. Its Capitol Complex is part of a UNESCO World Heritage listing. Visitors also enjoy the Rock Garden, built from recycled waste, and Sukhna Lake.
bestTime: October to March.

name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
overview: Formed in 2020 by merging two former Portuguese territories. Daman and Diu offer quiet beaches, sea forts and old churches on the Gujarat coast, while Dadra and Nagar Haveli is a forested, tribal region with rivers and gardens near Silvassa.
bestTime: October to March.

name: Delhi
overview: India's capital has been the seat of empires for centuries. It has three UNESCO World Heritage Sites (the Red Fort, Qutub Minar and Humayun's Tomb) alongside the busy lanes of Old Delhi, Lutyens' boulevards, modern temples and some of the country's best street food.
bestTime: October to March; winter mornings can be foggy and smoggy.

name: Jammu and Kashmir
overview: Often called paradise on earth, the Kashmir Valley offers houseboats on Dal Lake, Mughal gardens, and the meadows of Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg. In the Jammu region, pilgrims climb to the Vaishno Devi shrine. Gulmarg is India's best-known ski resort.
bestTime: March to October for the valley; December to February for snow.

name: Ladakh
overview: A high-altitude cold desert between the Karakoram and the Great Himalaya. Ladakh is known for Pangong Tso, Nubra Valley's sand dunes and Bactrian camels, centuries-old monasteries such as Hemis and Thiksey, and some of the world's highest motorable roads. Allow time to acclimatise on arrival.
bestTime: May to September, when the passes are open.

name: Lakshadweep
overview: India's smallest union territory is a group of coral islands and lagoons in the Arabian Sea. Only a few islands, such as Agatti, Bangaram and Kavaratti, are open to tourists, which keeps the reefs pristine for snorkelling, diving and kayaking. An entry permit is required.
bestTime: October to May.

name: Puducherry
overview: A former French colony on the Tamil Nadu coast. Puducherry's White Town has mustard-yellow villas, cafés and a seaside promenade. Nearby is Auroville, an experimental township built around the golden Matrimandir, and the Sri Aurobindo Ashram.
bestTime: October to March.
